name: Gloria Smith
home: the streets inland from Pier Beach
life: “My first passport photograph shows the earrings I sold to pay for the passport.” Tuesday often includes a stop at the corner outside Coastal Barber, where Gloria usually checks the board before the regulars give a more colorful account of the news.
voice: I kept a postage-stamp square. It fits inside the passport I could never afford when that boat was new.
appearance: Gloria has silver temples and a dark fringe, an aquiline nose and a square chin, and a favorite piece of clothing, a narrow-striped sweater. It usually goes with a train token tied to a zipper pull. When somebody else has the floor, Gloria rubs a thumb along the edge of the nearest pocket.
personality: Gloria feels a room through sound. A door slammed in high spirits can produce the same instant startle as an angry one, and it takes a little while to hear what actually follows.
agenda: To keep the little sail square in a passport finally put to use.
family: Cecilia Woods is Gloria’s first cousin once removed. Gloria makes room at the table. Cecilia brings whatever was actually growing or affordable that week. The meal sometimes produces a solution. Even when it does not, everyone goes away knowing what the other household is up against. Asked about *Two left slippers*, Cecilia says, “I bought my dad those slippers after he fell.”
connections: Daryl Mills. A shorebound neighbor can keep a piece of water as a shade or a passport square.
